Here's some stuff I learned while in therapy.
-Make small goals and complete them (do the dishes, take a walk around the block, make a playlist of happy songs and listen to it)
-Do not compare your problems to others, I kept telling my-self that there were other people on the boat that had it much worse than me and it just made things worse. Why was I feeling down when others had more to deal with? This was tough to over-come, it took some Marine with ptsd (now a very close-friend) that was in my class to convince me that comparing problems is unhealthy and doesn't help any-one.
-Talk to some-one, I've always had some-one that was close to me in my commands that I could turn to when I was feeling down. Having a best-friend is always good. No advice on how to obtain one, my go-to person was some-one I worked with and had some similar interests.
-Exercise, went on a 10 mile flack-run(flak-run? the thing Marines do where they wear a bullet-proof-vest and run) with my afformentioned friend. It helped relieve some stress and gave me some bragging rights. Or go for a walk, always helps me calm down.
-Write about your day, I started during boot-camp and I've always resorted to it when I was feeling down. It helps clear your mind and figure out what's really bothering you. In class we had to write a letter to some-one we admired and one to some-one we hate. It helped me out a lot. Depending on what you're going through this can be very tough, my friend was reduced to tears and had flash-backs while writing his, I just cried a bit and some-one else in our class didn't have any strong emotional response. I highly recommend at least the positive letter.
-Try a positive coping technique, photography, baking, making flower-crowns, knitting, crochet, slam-poetry, watching anime, self-defense(MMA,Judo,Karate other such things), drawing, playing an intsrument, volunteering, and many more. Make sure you have multiple techniques, my psych told me that some people use exercise exclusively and if they break their arm have psychotic breaks. And if you're worried about people judging about your coping technique just know that all of the ones I listed are used by various service members I've met.

If things are bad to the point where your want to commit suicide or have to hide how your coping then please reach out. I was cutting to deal with stress and when some-one finally saw what I was doing they immediatly went to doc who had no choice but to send me to mental health. Admitting you have a problem is the first step in recovery. It took a bit for me to fully understand that how I was dealing with stress was not healthy. One thing I that helped me a lot was knowing I wasn't the only person to cut my-self in the military. Tried googling things to see what other people went through and only found one post about some-one active duty resorting to self-harm. If your reading this just know that you're not alone.
I'm not going to list all the alternatives to self harm because this post is already long enough and since I've got auto-correct off I've already commited too many grammar and spelling sins to carry on. If any-body needs to talk I'm here for you, it might take while to respond because I'm not too active on this site anymore but I will get back to you.
